record.original_question: More generally, what smoothness can be proved for solutions of initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations in arbitrary spatial dimension?

evidence.quote: Much more generally, the open problem is to understand what can be said about smoothness of solutions of IBVP's for dispersive equations in any dimension. This problem seems to be largely unexplored.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and consider a dispersive partial differential equation posed on a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$ (for example, a half-space, a smooth bounded domain, or the exterior of a smooth obstacle). Typical model equations include:

- the linear Schrödinger equation $i\partial_t u + \Delta u = 0$,
- the linear or nonlinear Korteweg–de Vries-type and Zakharov–Kuznetsov-type equations,
- and other linear/nonlinear dispersive equations whose symbol $p(\xi)$ satisfies $|\nabla p(\xi)| \to \infty$ as $|\xi| \to \infty$.

The initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) consists of prescribing an initial datum $u(0,x) = u_0(x)$ for $x \in \Omega$ together with appropriate boundary conditions on $(0,T) \times \partial\Omega$ (e.g. Dirichlet, Neumann, or other admissible boundary data) so that the problem is well-posed in a suitable Sobolev space.

Determine, for general dispersive IBVPs in arbitrary spatial dimension $n$, the smoothness (interior and up-to-the-boundary regularity) that solutions $u(t,x)$ must possess. More precisely:

(a) Identify the local and global smoothing effects (gain of regularity in space and/or time) for solutions of such IBVPs as a function of the regularity of the initial data $u_0$ and the boundary data, generalizing the Kato-type local smoothing known for the Cauchy problem on $\mathbb{R}^n$.

(b) Characterize the propagation of regularity from subdomains of $\Omega$ (or from portions of the boundary) into the rest of $\Omega$ for $t > 0$.

(c) Determine sharp Sobolev (or Besov) regularity classes in which the IBVP is well-posed in $n \geq 2$ dimensions, particularly for nonlinear models of KdV, Zakharov–Kuznetsov, and Schrödinger type on domains with boundary.
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of smoothness of solutions to initial-boundary value problems for dispersive equations in arbitrary spatial dimension remains largely open. Recent work has established partial results: smoothing and propagation-of-regularity results for specific equations (KdV-type, Zakharov–Kuznetsov, two-dimensional Kawahara, Schrödinger) and on bounded intervals or special domains, but no general theory in arbitrary dimension is currently available.

status_evidence.title: Smoothing properties for a two-dimensional Kawahara equation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies smoothing for a 2D dispersive equation, indicating progress in higher dimension is recent and case-by-case.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional smoothing results exist only for specific dispersive models, not as a general theory.

status_evidence.title: Initial-Boundary Value Problems for Nonlinear Dispersive Equations of Higher Orders Posed on Bounded Intervals
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and regularity for IBVPs on bounded intervals (1D).
status_evidence.claim: Most rigorous IBVP regularity results remain in one spatial dimension.

status_evidence.title: The propagation of regularity and dispersive blow-up phenomenon to higher-order generalized KdV equations
status_evidence.snippet: Propagation of regularity for higher-order KdV in 1D Cauchy setting.
status_evidence.claim: Propagation-of-regularity results have been extended to additional models but remain partial.
